successCriteria.description: knexfile.ts exports a Knex config that reads DATABASE_URL from environment and supports TypeScript migrations (ts-node or tsx for migration files)
src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts exports a LeaveType interface with fields: id (string), code (string), label (string), description (string), isActive (boolean), createdAt (Date), updatedAt (Date)

src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts exports ILeaveTypeRepository interface with methods: findAll() → Promise<LeaveType[]>, findById(id: string) → Promise<LeaveType | null>, findByCode(code: string) → Promise<LeaveType | null>, create(input: { code, label, description, isActive }) → Promise<LeaveType>

KnexLeaveTypeRepository class implements ILeaveTypeRepository, accepts a Knex instance via constructor, and maps snake_case DB columns (is_active, created_at, updated_at) to camelCase LeaveType fields

migrations/001_create_leave_types.ts: up creates leave_types table with columns id (uuid PK), code (varchar unique not null), label (varchar not null), description (text), is_active (boolean default true), created_at (timestamptz), updated_at (timestamptz); down drops the table

Existing unit test at tests/unit/modules/leave/leave-type.repository.test.ts passes: findAll returns only active types, findById returns type or null, findByCode returns type or null, create inserts and returns new type

constraints: GP-001: All database access for leave_types must go through KnexLeaveTypeRepository — no inline Knex calls in models, services, or controllers
HARNESS.json constraint 'no-any': Use unknown with type guards instead of any in all new code
HARNESS.json constraint 'no-direct-db-outside-repository': Knex instance only used inside KnexLeaveTypeRepository; other modules import the interface
HARNESS.json constraint 'no-hardcoded-secrets': DATABASE_URL read from environment only, never hardcoded in knexfile.ts
KnexLeaveTypeRepository constructor must accept a Knex instance (dependency injection), not import db directly — the test file already mocks Knex and expects constructor injection
outOfScope: LeaveService with business logic for submit/approve/reject/cancel (Phase 4)
Seed scripts for default leave types (Phase 6)
LeaveBalanceService, balance routes, barrel exports, and integration tests (Phases 7-9)
Audit logging (GP-002) — not required for this phase since LeaveType is a static catalog entity with no state-changing operations in scope

ambiguities.description: Table name conflict: ARCHITECTURE.md specifies the table as `leave_type` (singular), but the intent text, migration filename (001_create_leave_types), and the existing test file all use `leave_types` (plural). The test asserts `knexFn).toHaveBeenCalledWith('leave_types')`. Which name should the migration and repository use?
options: Use `leave_types` (plural) — matches intent, migration filename, and existing test
Use `leave_type` (singular) — matches ARCHITECTURE.md canonical table specification

ambiguities.description: The intent says knexfile.ts should have "TypeScript support for migrations" but does not specify the loader (ts-node vs tsx). Knex typically uses ts-node with the `--require ts-node/register` flag or the `tsx` package. The choice affects the knexfile migration configuration and devDependencies.
